name: Gaussian Splat
summary: One picture becomes a 3D Gaussian splat: Idol/TripoSplat writes the .spz, a .glb mesh and a turntable clip.

source.notes: Converted with tools/import_workflow.py (the subgraphs are flattened by tools/ui2api.py), then the two SaveGLB exports and the subgraph's background, gaussian-count and preview switches were exposed as app inputs. The .spz splat, the .glb mesh and the orbit clip are all kept.

inputs.label: Picture
inputs.help: One subject, well lit, alone on its background: the splat is built from what it sees.

inputs.label: Remove background
inputs.help: Cut the subject out with BiRefNet before the splat is built. Turn it off when the picture already has an alpha channel.

inputs.label: Gaussians
inputs.help: How many points the splat holds. 262k matches Idol's octree density; more points are denser, not more detailed, and cost time and VRAM.

inputs.label: Sampling preview
inputs.help: Draw the sampling preview while the splat decodes. Off is a little faster and uses less VRAM.

inputs.label: Steps
inputs.help: Diffusion steps. 20 is the workflow's default; fewer is a rougher draft, more a slower refinement.

inputs.label: Seed
inputs.help: -1 picks a random seed for the sampler.

inputs.label: Turntable frames
inputs.help: The orbit clip runs at 25 fps: 75 frames is 3 seconds, 250 is 10.

credits: Idol by Comfy-Org (Apache-2.0), a fine-tune of TripoSplat by VAST-AI-Research
notes: Idol is Comfy-Org's fine-tune of TripoSplat. The picture is cut out (BiRefNet), encoded with DINOv3, denoised into a sparse gaussian set (Idol + the Idol decoder) and decoded to a splat. The app writes the native .spz splat, a triangle-mesh .glb and a 25 fps turntable render of the splat. The .glb opens in the viewer here, Blender, Godot or Unity; the .spz opens in gaussian-splat viewers such as SuperSplat. 262k gaussians matches the octree density; more is denser, not more detailed. One subject per picture works best; the seed changes the sampler and the gaussian layout.
